question: Should ClawSweeper own the proposed advisory release-train reporting lane beyond the local read-only audit, including state publication and non-blocking release-branch Check Runs?
rationale: The remaining work defines new release-governance and automation responsibilities; code inspection cannot decide whether that responsibility belongs in ClawSweeper or what permanent policy contract maintainers want.

options.title: Sponsor the staged advisory lane
options.body: Approve the non-blocking direction, review the audit foundation first, and require separate publishing/check changes plus a complete shadow train before considering enforcement.

options.title: Limit scope to local audit
options.body: Allow only the deterministic local reporting command and defer durable publication, Check Runs, dashboards, and enforcement indefinitely.

options.title: Keep release governance external
options.body: Decline the new ClawSweeper lane and retain release-train scope decisions and reporting in maintainer documentation or other release tooling.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged advisory lane
recommendation.body: Approve the non-blocking direction, review the audit foundation first, and require separate publishing/check changes plus a complete shadow train before considering enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the best available repository-policy routing candidate for deciding whether ClawSweeper should assume this additional automation responsibility.
